caption: The image shows a rectangular plaque with an arched top, appearing to be made of a grey or weathered stone or metal. At the top center within the arch, there is a carved image of a sun with radiating rays. Below the arch, the upper section of the plaque is divided into two main vertical panels by three pillars, each decorated with vertical grooves. The left panel contains a cluster of carved flowers or leaves above a circular motif that encloses a heart with a lattice pattern; the number "7" is to the right of the heart, and the number "1" is to the left. The right panel contains a similar cluster of carved flowers or leaves above the number "6" on the left and the number "3" on the right, together forming the date "1763." Between the two upper panels, above the pillars, is a smaller depiction of a plant, possibly a flower, with curling leaves. Beneath these elements, there is a horizontal band containing a carved inscription in capital letters that reads "COLEBROOKDALE FURNACE." The lower portion of the plaque is largely plain, except for a pattern of small diamond shapes arranged in a larger diamond formation at the center. The overall color is monochromatic grey, consistent with aged or oxidized metal, giving the drawing a subdued appearance.
title: Stove Plate
